brief: Carlos Zapata’s asymmetric lotus tower with a floor-by-floor curved glazed exterior, inclined upper leaf, projecting oval helipad with open safety net, lower mechanical belt and glazed retail podium under its floating steel canopy.

nativeAxes.longitudinal: +Z toward the mapped southern helipad projection
nativeAxes.origin: Exact-QID mapped outer envelope center; tower center is offset to the west of the podium.

sourceFacts.heightSource: Council on Vertical Urbanism / Skyscraper Center
sourceFacts.facadeSource: Meinhardt Facade Technology: inward taper at lower 20 floors, bespoke panels, 22 m helipad cantilever.
sourceFacts.sourceDiscrepancies: Turner178m is49th-floor observation deck, not helipad; registry181.9m observatory differs. Turner52nd/registry55th helipad floor labels differ; registry191.4m helipad height governs. Five retailstories versus sixlevels retained as different counts. OSM269m roofpart rejected against262.5m published architectural height.

reconstruction.plan: Northern tower cusp, podium outline and rooftop landing marking are registered in the exact-QID map frame. The outer mapped southern lobe contains the helipad projection and is not blindly used as a shaft footprint. Smooth typical-floor lens controls and profile samples reconstruct the published plan and public engineering photographs; dimensioned floor drawings remain unavailable.
reconstruction.upperLeaf: Inclined cut across the changing floor perimeter, closed by a separate framed front; crown plane and profile are reconstructed.

helipad.note: Oval deck plan and soffit thickness are reconstructed around the mapped landing square; cantilever and orientation need comparison with construction drawings.
